We have people working all over the world, including Canada, Spain, Switzerland, the United Kingdom, the United States and more!\n\n\n\nAs a senior technology leader, you will help build our technology platform to enable 10 million change-makers to deliver a billion acts of goodness by 2025. We seek a platform-first Architect to lead enterprise patterns for reliable, governed, AI-driven, and cost-effective solutions at scale across our technology portfolio. You will design how data flows across the company, from ingestion to consumption, while ensuring our AI systems are secure, auditable, and maintainable. This role requires practical systems thinking and the ability to influence senior engineers and leadership toward consistent, enterprise-wide architecture outcomes that align our data and AI strategy with broader business goals.\n\nIf you're passionate about leveraging modern technology, data and AI for positive impact and eager to contribute to a mission-driven organization, we want to hear from you.\n\n\n\nWhat you will do:\n\n - Develop and maintain end-to-end tracks with our data and AI focus technology strategy and architectural portfolio\n\n - Mentor engineers and technical leadership by providing clear patterns, ensuring adherence to architectural patterns, and offering hands-on guidance for complex implementations\n\n - Lead architecture decisioning through Architecture Decision Records (ADRs), standards, and design reviews\n\n - Oversee architectural reviews, code reviews, and system performance analysis to ensure quality standards and sustainable delivery momentum\n\n - Foster a culture of collaboration, knowledge sharing, and continuous learning through mentorship, team collaboration, and workshops\n\n - Enable governed data consumption through clear data contracts, curated datasets, and consistent serving patterns including domain marts\n\n - Standardize end-to-end data flow patterns including ingestion, transformation, storage, serving, and retirement with repeatable templates\n\n - Set platform standards for orchestration and reliability including SLAs, retries, idempotency, backfills, runbooks, and operational dashboards\n\n - Establish enterprise data quality practices including critical data elements, quality rules, validation layers, monitoring, and issue triage workflows\n\n - Drive governance-by-design by embedding metadata, lineage, classification, and ownership into platform patterns\n\n - Drive adoption of AI governance architecture for agentic solutions including controls for data privacy and model lifecycle\n\n - Define AIOps standards ensuring AI systems have traceability, quality measurement, incident response readiness, and cost guardrails\n\n - Collaborate with stakeholders and product management to identify, prioritize, and mitigate technical risks and challenges\n\n - Stay informed about industry regulations, security standards, and compliance requirements to ensure solutions meet necessary standards\n\n\n\nWhat you’ll bring:\n\n - Bachelor's or Master's degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering, or a related field\n\n - 7+ years in software development methodologies, architecture, and implementation of large scale enterprise systems\n\n - 4+ years focused on data engineering, data management, or data platform architecture and designing AI solutions including AIOps practices\n\n - Structured problem solving to turn ambiguous requirements into scalable, low-cost solution patterns\n\n - Ability to think strategically while paying close attention to technical details\n\n - Proven experience building or evolving an enterprise data platform including standards and adoption across multiple teams\n\n - Demonstrated ability to design governance-ready AI solutions including evaluation strategies, privacy safeguards, and auditability\n\n - Strong expertise in system architecture, cloud computing, distributed systems, and integration technologies\n\n - High bar for operational readiness, actionable documentation, and treating governance as a built-in platform feature\n\n - Deep experience across modern data platform capabilities including AWS Glue, Step Functions, Airflow, dbt, Spark, and Snowflake\n\n - Proficiency in programming and analytics using Python, SQL, and Jupyter Notebooks\n\n - Experience with agentic frameworks such as LangChain, LlamaIndex, or LangGraph and AIOps tooling like LangFuse\n\n - Familiarity with Agile development methodologies and the ability to adapt to a fast-paced environment\n\n - Strong understanding of security principles, performance optimization, scalability, and reliability\n\n - Demonstrated influence towards simplicity and repeatability in architecture\n\n\n\nNice to Have:\n\n - Experience operating in regulated environments, (SOC2, ISO 27001, or GDPR).\n\n - Familiarity with federated domain ownership models, where domains ship data products while the platform provides shared standards and tooling.\n\n - Experience designing and scaling platform observability for data pipelines, streaming systems, and AI services.\n\n - Familiarity with medallion architecture patterns\n\n - Experience in modern data platform capabilities, including:\n   \n   - Streaming: Apache Kafka, AWS MSK, AWS Kinesis, GCP Pub/Sub\n   \n   - Metadata and governance: DataHub, Atlan or similar\n\n\nDISCOVER YOUR PURPOSE AT WORK\n\nWe’re not employees, we’re Benevity-ites. Through giving, volunteering, grantmaking, employee resource groups and micro-actions, we help most of the Fortune 100 brands build better cultures and use their power for good. We’re also one of the first B Corporations in Canada, meaning we’re as committed to purpose as we are to profits. We have people working all over the world, including Canada, Spain, Switzerland, the United Kingdom, the United States and more!\n\n\n\nAs a senior technology leader, you will help build our technology platform to enable 10 million change-makers to deliver a billion acts of goodness by 2025. We seek a platform-first Architect to lead enterprise patterns for reliable, governed, AI-driven, and cost-effective solutions at scale across our technology portfolio. You will design how data flows across the company, from ingestion to consumption, while ensuring our AI systems are secure, auditable, and maintainable. This role requires practical systems thinking and the ability to influence senior engineers and leadership toward consistent, enterprise-wide architecture outcomes that align our data and AI strategy with broader business goals.\n\nIf you're passionate about leveraging modern technology, data and AI for positive impact and eager to contribute to a mission-driven organization, we want to hear from you.\n\n\n\nWhat you will do:\n\n - Develop and maintain end-to-end tracks with our data and AI focus technology strategy and architectural portfolio\n\n - Mentor engineers and technical leadership by providing clear patterns, ensuring adherence to architectural patterns, and offering hands-on guidance for complex implementations\n\n - Lead architecture decisioning through Architecture Decision Records (ADRs), standards, and design reviews\n\n - Oversee architectural reviews, code reviews, and system performance analysis to ensure quality standards and sustainable delivery momentum\n\n - Foster a culture of collaboration, knowledge sharing, and continuous learning through mentorship, team collaboration, and workshops\n\n - Enable governed data consumption through clear data contracts, curated datasets, and consistent serving patterns including domain marts\n\n - Standardize end-to-end data flow patterns including ingestion, transformation, storage, serving, and retirement with repeatable templates\n\n - Set platform standards for orchestration and reliability including SLAs, retries, idempotency, backfills, runbooks, and operational dashboards\n\n - Establish enterprise data quality practices including critical data elements, quality rules, validation layers, monitoring, and issue triage workflows\n\n - Drive governance-by-design by embedding metadata, lineage, classification, and ownership into platform patterns\n\n - That unique combination of financial services and social mission creates a compliance profile that is anything but ordinary. The Sr. GRC Analyst will own, among other things, the governance layer of Benevity’s AML compliance program, including the policy framework, risk-based assessments , and training architecture translating regulatory obligations into documented, operational controls capable of withstanding regulatory scrutiny.\n\nReporting to the Sr. Manager, GRC and working in close partnership with other internal  teams, you will author and maintain Benevity’s AML program documentation, lead the program effectiveness review, build and deliver the annual compliance training curriculum, and own the company’s FINTRAC compliance governance structure and examination readiness posture. Lead the biennial program effectiveness review as required under PCMLTFA s.9.6, coordinating with internal stakeholders to assess and evidence program adequacy.\n\n - Maintain MSB registration standing and support the CCO operating cadence in partnership with the General Counsel.\n\n - Manage the AML compliance documentation suite, ensuring currency and consistency across the document suite, including being  audit-ready at all times.\n   \n\nFINTRAC Regulatory Engagement & Examination Readiness\n\n - Own Benevity’s FINTRAC examination readiness posture, maintaining a continuous state of preparedness that withstands regulatory scrutiny.\n\n - Coordinate remediation evidence development and closure in partnership with our Fraud and Finance teams, ensuring all examination findings are addressed with documented, defensible evidence packages.\n\n - Develop and maintain an examination response strategy, including communication and escalation protocols for regulatory engagement events.\n\n - Serve as a primary coordination point for FINTRAC inquiries, supported by internal and external AML counsel as appropriate.\n   \n\nPolicy Authoring & Risk-Based Methodology\n\n - Conduct and document risk-based assessments of Benevity’s ML/TF exposure, incorporating product, client, geographic, and delivery channel risk factors.\n\n - Develop supporting procedures for elevated-risk client and product scenarios in coordination with our Fraud and Finance teams and Legal.\n\n - Ensure documentation reflects the current state of operations and remains actionable rather than aspirational.\n\nCompliance Training Design & Delivery\n\n - Design, build, and deliver Benevity’s annual AML compliance training program, calibrated by role and function to reflect actual risk exposure.\n\n - Maintain training completion records and reporting to support examination readiness and demonstrate regulatory compliance.\n\n - Develop targeted content for functions with elevated AML exposure, including client operations, finance, and onboarding.\n\n - Assess training effectiveness and iterate on curriculum to reflect regulatory developments and lessons learned from operational events.\n   \n\nRegulatory Horizon Scanning & Advisory\n\n - Monitor and synthesize regulatory developments across FINTRAC, FinCEN, BSA, OFAC,, providing timely horizon scanning outputs to GRC leadership and the General Counsel.\n\n - Track regulatory guidance, enforcement trends, and examination priorities that affect Benevity’s business model, client base, and charitable disbursement operations.\n\n - Advise the business on the compliance implications of product changes, new market entry, and client onboarding scenarios, translating regulatory risk into actionable guidance.\n\nTooling, Automation & Advisory\n\n - Leverage AI tools and automation as a force multiplier, accelerating policy gap analysis, regulatory monitoring, evidence packaging, and training development to scale program output without scaling headcount.\n\n - Maintain compliance program documentation and workflow tracking in OneTrust, ensuring the GRC toolset reflects the current state of the AML program.\n\n - Contribute to Benevity’s broader GRC program as a subject matter expert, supporting cross-functional audits, control testing, and regulatory filings as needed.\n\n - Familiarity with BSA, FinCEN, and OFAC frameworks and their applicability in a cross-border, multi-jurisdiction context.\n\n - Experience preparing for or supporting regulatory examinations, with the ability to organize evidence and coordinate stakeholders under deadline pressure.\n\n - Strong writing and communication skills, with the ability to produce compliance documentation that is clear, precise, and defensible.\n\n - Comfort working across organizational boundaries, particularly with operational teams and Legal, where the lines between program governance and execution need to stay well-defined.\n\n - The ideal candidate is a confident cross functional leader who can build programs, influence without authority, and translate policy into practice across a complex data organization.</p><p style=\"min-height:1.5em\"></p><p style=\"min-height:1.5em\"><strong>What you'll do:</strong></p><ul style=\"min-height:1.5em\"><li><p style=\"min-height:1.5em\">Lead and grow the Data Governance function, setting the strategic direction for data ownership, stewardship policy, access governance, and data classification standards across the organization.</p></li><li><p style=\"min-height:1.5em\">Own and operate DataHub as the living catalog of the organization's data assets, covering metadata management, catalog onboarding, tagging, lineage registration, and domain stewardship.</p></li><li><p style=\"min-height:1.5em\">Extend the governance toolchain beyond DataHub by evaluating and deploying complementary platforms such as Collibra, Alation, or Atlan for policy management and business glossary; Monte Carlo or Lightup for data observability; OneTrust or Privacera for privacy and entitlement governance; and Great Expectations or dbt tests for quality rule enforcement.</p></li><li><p style=\"min-height:1.5em\">Own the enterprise Data Quality Framework, defining six quality dimensions that apply across all functions: Completeness, Accuracy, Timeliness, Consistency, Validity, and Uniqueness.</p></li><li><p style=\"min-height:1.5em\">Classify every data asset into a quality tier: Tier 1 for business critical, Tier 2 for operational, Tier 3 for exploratory. SLAs and enforcement standards are documented, visible, and enforced by tier.</p></li><li><p style=\"min-height:1.5em\">Formally document data quality SLAs per domain and per tier, publish them in DataHub, and review them on a biannual cadence.</p></li><li><p style=\"min-height:1.5em\">Define and publish a data health score methodology. Domain health scores are visible in the catalog and reported monthly to the data domain council.</p></li><li><p style=\"min-height:1.5em\">Conduct quarterly data quality audits across all functions, share findings with the domain council, and assign remediation with named accountability and due dates.</p></li><li><p style=\"min-height:1.5em\">Define and maintain the profiling policy: which datasets are profiled, how often, and what thresholds trigger an escalation. This is never left to individual interpretation.</p></li><li><p style=\"min-height:1.5em\">Govern the separation between defining quality rules and implementing them. Governance defines. Engineering and DataOps implement. When a breach occurs, Governance escalates to the owning function and tracks resolution.</p></li><li><p style=\"min-height:1.5em\">Own access control and entitlements governance, ensuring data sensitivity classifications are applied and access is granted and revoked in accordance with policy.</p></li><li><p style=\"min-height:1.5em\">Lead compliance alignment across privacy regulations, internal audit requirements, and industry standards. Partner with Legal and Security to ensure data handling practices are always current.</p></li><li><p style=\"min-height:1.5em\">Facilitate the cross functional data domain council, driving alignment across data owners, stewards, and platform teams on standards, escalations, and roadmap priorities.</p></li><li><p style=\"min-height:1.5em\">Build a culture of data accountability across the organization through training, communication, and stakeholder engagement programs.</p></li></ul><p style=\"min-height:1.5em\"></p><p style=\"min-height:1.5em\"><strong>What you'll bring:</strong></p><ul style=\"min-height:1.5em\"><li><p style=\"min-height:1.5em\">Degree in Computer Science, Information Management, Business, or equivalent professional experience.</p></li><li><p style=\"min-height:1.5em\">7 or more years of experience in data governance, data management, or a closely related field, with at least 2 years in a people or program leadership role.</p></li><li><p style=\"min-height:1.5em\">Hands on experience operating a data catalog or metadata management platform. Experience with DataHub is strongly preferred. Familiarity with Collibra, Alation, or Atlan is a significant asset.</p></li><li><p style=\"min-height:1.5em\">Working knowledge of data observability and quality tooling, including platforms such as Monte Carlo, Lightup, Great Expectations, or dbt.</p></li><li><p style=\"min-height:1.5em\">Familiarity with privacy and entitlement governance platforms such as OneTrust, Privacera, or equivalent.</p></li><li><p style=\"min-height:1.5em\">Strong understanding of data quality frameworks, including how to define dimensions, set SLAs, build health scores, and drive remediation.</p></li><li><p style=\"min-height:1.5em\">Experience designing and enforcing data classification schemes and access governance frameworks in a cloud environment (AWS, Azure, or GCP).</p></li><li><p style=\"min-height:1.5em\">Solid understanding of regulatory and compliance requirements relevant to data, including GDPR, CCPA, SOC 2, and internal audit standards.</p></li><li><p style=\"min-height:1.5em\">Demonstrated ability to facilitate cross functional councils or governance bodies, drive alignment among opinionated stakeholders, and hold teams accountable to standards.</p></li><li><p style=\"min-height:1.5em\">Strong communication skills. You can write a policy, present findings to an executive audience, and translate data governance concepts into language that non technical stakeholders act on.</p></li><li><p style=\"min-height:1.5em\">Experience working with dbt and understanding how lineage, documentation, and testing practices connect to governance outcomes.</p></li><li><p style=\"min-height:1.5em\">Ability to build programs from the ground up and operate in an environment where governance practices are still maturing.</p></li></ul><p style=\"min-height:1.5em\"></p><p style=\"min-height:1.5em\"><strong>Great-to-haves:</strong></p><ul style=\"min-height:1.5em\"><li><p style=\"min-height:1.5em\">DAMA Certified Data Management Professional (CDMP) certification</p></li><li><p style=\"min-height:1.5em\">Experience with DataHub Cloud or Acryl Data</p></li><li><p style=\"min-height:1.5em\">Familiarity with Apache Atlas or AWS Glue Data Catalog</p></li><li><p style=\"min-height:1.5em\">Experience building data governance programs in a SaaS or B2B technology company</p></li><li><p style=\"min-height:1.5em\">Exposure to MLOps governance or AI model risk frameworks</p></li></ul><h2><strong>Discover your purpose at work</strong></h2><p style=\"min-height:1.5em\">We’re not employees, we’re Benevity-ites. Through giving, volunteering, grantmaking, employee resource groups and micro-actions, we help most of the Fortune 100 brands build better cultures and use their power for good. We’re also one of the first B Corporations in Canada, meaning we’re as committed to purpose as we are to profits. We have people working all over the world, including Canada, Spain, Switzerland, the United Kingdom, the United States and more!\n\n\n\nBenevity's software architecture has evolved to include a diverse technology stack. The front end application, using mainly VueJS, is designed for both desktop and mobile web rendering. Our back end systems (some Java SpringBoot, some PHP) manage data processing, interfaces with external providers, and ensures robust security. We run and operate our systems in AWS and GCP cloud, leveraging where possible cloud native technology. We emphasize clean, maintainable code and use GIT for version control and collaboration. Additionally, our platform integrates with various external services for functionalities like email communication, content storage, and server to server interactions.\n\nOur culture is driven by our core value of \"we are we\" and as a Manager of Data Governance you will work in an outcome driven environment where collaboration with your product, design and engineering counterparts is paramount.\n\nIf you are eager to make a difference and thrive in a collaborative setting, we invite you to join our team!\n\n\n\nPosition Overview:\n\nData Governance exists so that the rest of the organization can trust what they are working with. The Manager of Data Governance sets the rules, owns the standards, and holds everyone accountable. This role is the organizational authority on what data exists, who owns it, where it came from, and who can access it. On quality specifically, this team defines what good looks like. Engineering and DataOps make it happen. Governance checks whether it actually did. The ideal candidate is a confident cross functional leader who can build programs, influence without authority, and translate policy into practice across a complex data organization.\n\n\n\nWhat you'll do:\n\n - Lead and grow the Data Governance function, setting the strategic direction for data ownership, stewardship policy, access governance, and data classification standards across the organization.\n\n - Own and operate DataHub as the living catalog of the organization's data assets, covering metadata management, catalog onboarding, tagging, lineage registration, and domain stewardship.\n\n - Extend the governance toolchain beyond DataHub by evaluating and deploying complementary platforms such as Collibra, Alation, or Atlan for policy management and business glossary; Monte Carlo or Lightup for data observability; OneTrust or Privacera for privacy and entitlement governance; and Great Expectations or dbt tests for quality rule enforcement.\n\n - Own the enterprise Data Quality Framework, defining six quality dimensions that apply across all functions: Completeness, Accuracy, Timeliness, Consistency, Validity, and Uniqueness.\n\n - Classify every data asset into a quality tier: Tier 1 for business critical, Tier 2 for operational, Tier 3 for exploratory. SLAs and enforcement standards are documented, visible, and enforced by tier.\n\n - Formally document data quality SLAs per domain and per tier, publish them in DataHub, and review them on a biannual cadence.\n\n - Define and publish a data health score methodology. Domain health scores are visible in the catalog and reported monthly to the data domain council.\n\n - Conduct quarterly data quality audits across all functions, share findings with the domain council, and assign remediation with named accountability and due dates.\n\n - Define and maintain the profiling policy: which datasets are profiled, how often, and what thresholds trigger an escalation. This is never left to individual interpretation.\n\n - Govern the separation between defining quality rules and implementing them. Governance defines. Engineering and DataOps implement. When a breach occurs, Governance escalates to the owning function and tracks resolution.\n\n - Own access control and entitlements governance, ensuring data sensitivity classifications are applied and access is granted and revoked in accordance with policy.\n\n - Lead compliance alignment across privacy regulations, internal audit requirements, and industry standards. Partner with Legal and Security to ensure data handling practices are always current.\n\n - Facilitate the cross functional data domain council, driving alignment across data owners, stewards, and platform teams on standards, escalations, and roadmap priorities.\n\n - Build a culture of data accountability across the organization through training, communication, and stakeholder engagement programs.\n\n\n\nWhat you'll bring:\n\n - Degree in Computer Science, Information Management, Business, or equivalent professional experience.\n\n - 7 or more years of experience in data governance, data management, or a closely related field, with at least 2 years in a people or program leadership role.\n\n - Hands on experience operating a data catalog or metadata management platform. Experience with DataHub is strongly preferred. Familiarity with Collibra, Alation, or Atlan is a significant asset.\n\n - Working knowledge of data observability and quality tooling, including platforms such as Monte Carlo, Lightup, Great Expectations, or dbt.\n\n - Familiarity with privacy and entitlement governance platforms such as OneTrust, Privacera, or equivalent.\n\n - Strong understanding of data quality frameworks, including how to define dimensions, set SLAs, build health scores, and drive remediation.\n\n - Experience designing and enforcing data classification schemes and access governance frameworks in a cloud environment (AWS, Azure, or GCP).\n\n - Solid understanding of regulatory and compliance requirements relevant to data, including GDPR, CCPA, SOC 2, and internal audit standards.\n\n - Demonstrated ability to facilitate cross functional councils or governance bodies, drive alignment among opinionated stakeholders, and hold teams accountable to standards.\n\n - Strong communication skills. You can write a policy, present findings to an executive audience, and translate data governance concepts into language that non technical stakeholders act on.\n\n - Experience working with dbt and understanding how lineage, documentation, and testing practices connect to governance outcomes.\n\n - Ability to build programs from the ground up and operate in an environment where governance practices are still maturing.\n\n\n\nGreat-to-haves:\n\n - DAMA Certified Data Management Professional (CDMP) certification\n\n - Experience with DataHub Cloud or Acryl Data\n\n - Familiarity with Apache Atlas or AWS Glue Data Catalog\n\n - Experience building data governance programs in a SaaS or B2B technology company\n\n - Exposure to MLOps governance or AI model risk frameworks\n\n\nDISCOVER YOUR PURPOSE AT WORK\n\nWe’re not employees, we’re Benevity-ites. Embed security into the SDLC via CI/CD automation, SAST/SCA/DAST tooling, secure API patterns, and threat modeling.\n\n - Maintain the enterprise security risk register and vulnerability management lifecycle, prioritizing remediation by real-world risk.\n\n - Practical understanding of AI and LLM security risks, including the OWASP Top 10 for LLMs, prompt injection and the security implications of agentic systems\n\n - A clear, evidence-based point of view on where AI adds value in security work, where it falls short, and how to get it production-ready — and the curiosity to keep revising that view as the tooling changes\n\n - Working knowledge of SAST, SCA, DAST, API and microservices security, proven ability to set direction and evaluate the quality of the work\n\n - Deep understanding of cloud security, threat detection and modern attacker tactics, techniques and procedures in containerized, API-driven environments. Additionally, you will define how Benevity secures its AI-powered product capabilities and shapes the adoption of AI tooling to accelerate our internal security practice.\n\nWhat you’ll do:\n\n - Lead and coach a multi-disciplinary security team, driving team development, hiring, and a sustainable operating cadence.\n\n - Own critical security KPIs and ensure continuous improvement on various metrics to improve Benevity’s security posture.\n\n - Drive the information security roadmap and manage security vendors, aligning execution directly with CISO strategy and direction.\n\n - Oversee end-to-end security operations and incident response, serving as the senior escalation lead during major events.\n\n - Hold external security partners (including MDR providers) accountable for high-fidelity coverage, triage quality, and rapid response.\n\n - Establish AI security standards for LLM integrations, RAG pipelines, and agentic workflows using frameworks like OWASP and MITRE ATLAS.\n\n - Operationalize AI within the security team to enhance triage, threat detection, investigation, and reporting capabilities.\n\n - Embed security into the SDLC via CI/CD automation, SAST/SCA/DAST tooling, secure API patterns, and threat modeling.\n\n - Maintain the enterprise security risk register and vulnerability management lifecycle, prioritizing remediation by real-world risk.\n\n - 10+ years of progressive experience in information security, including 5+ years leading teams\n\n - Experience managing managers as well as individual contributors, with a track record of developing both\n\n - Breadth across security operations, product and application security, and cloud security Hands-on experience managing security operations on AWS, and other cloud providers.\n\n - Hands-on experience leading major incident response, including acting as incident commander, coordinating cross-functional responders and managing communications under pressure\n\n - Practical understanding of AI and LLM security risks, including the OWASP Top 10 for LLMs, prompt injection and the security implications of agentic systems\n\n - A clear, evidence-based point of view on where AI adds value in security work, where it falls short, and how to get it production-ready — and the curiosity to keep revising that view as the tooling changes\n\n - Working knowledge of SAST, SCA, DAST, API and microservices security, proven ability to set direction and evaluate the quality of the work\n\n - Deep understanding of cloud security, threat detection and modern attacker tactics, techniques and procedures in containerized, API-driven environments.
